edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 2, Paris 1844), De praescriptionibus adversus haereticos, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Ergo non ad Scripturas provocandum est; nec in his constituendum certamen, in quibus aut nulla, aut incerta victoria est, aut par incertae. Nam etsi non ita evaderet conlatio Scripturarum, ut utramque partem parem sisteret, ordo rerum desiderabat illud prius proponi, quod nunc solum disputandum est: Quibus competat fides ipsa? Cujus sint Scripturae? A quo, et per quos, et quando, et quibus sit tradita disciplina qua fiunt christiani? Ubi enim apparuerit esse veritatem et disciplinae et fidei christianae, illic erit veritas Scripturarum, et expositionum, et omnium traditionum christianarum.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore it is not to the Scriptures that appeal must be made; nor in these is the contest to be established, in which either no victory or uncertain victory or equal uncertain victory is. For even if the comparison of Scriptures did not turn out in such a way that it would set both parts equal, the order of things required that that be proposed first, which now alone is to be disputed: To whom does the faith itself belong? Of whom are the Scriptures? From whom, and through whom, and when, and to whom was the discipline by which Christians are made handed down? For where the truth of the Christian discipline and faith will have appeared, there will be the truth of the Scriptures, and of the explanations, and of all Christian traditions.

choices.english: To whom does the faith itself belong

pass_b_english: Therefore we must not appeal to the Scriptures, nor set the contest in them, where the outcome is either no victory, an uncertain one, or a tie that is equally uncertain. Even if a comparison of the Scriptures did not end up leveling both sides, the logical order demanded that the primary question be raised first—the only question now at issue: To whom does the faith itself belong? Whose are the Scriptures? From whom, through whom, when, and to whom was the discipline that makes Christians handed down? For wherever the truth of Christian discipline and faith appears, there will be the truth of the Scriptures, of their interpretations, and of all Christian traditions.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The distinction in 'provocandum est' (passive/impersonal) is handled well in both, and the logical flow regarding the priority of the question of authority over the comparison of texts is preserved.
